Describing your week: the toolbox

No new rule today: you put together what you already know to describe a typical week. In Italian, habits are told in the simple present tense.

To say…In ItalianThe trap for English speakers
what you dolavoro, leggo, dormo, finiscono subject: lavoro = I work
your routinemi alzo, ti svegli, si riposaI get up = mi alzo, never \"io alzo\"
the timealle sette, all'unaat seven = alle sette: the article is required
the usual dayil lunedì, la domenicail lunedì = every Monday; lunedì alone = that particular Monday
frequencysempre, spesso, di solito, non… mainon lavoro mai: non + mai, both required
descriptionuna settimana lunga, molte riunionithe adjective follows the noun and agrees

Today's rule: a typical week is told in the present, with the day or the time, then the verb, then the rest of the sentence.

", "

Building a complete sentence

The word order is close to English, with two differences: the negation non and the pronoun (mi, ti, si) go before the verb; sempre, spesso and mai go right after it.

Whennonpronounverbfrequencyrest
Il lunedìmialzosemprealle sei e mezza.
La domenicanonmisvegliomaipresto.
Il venerdì seranonlavoromai.
Di solito ceno alle otto, poi leggo.I usually have dinner at eight, then I read.

Molto: invariable or agreeing?

Before an adjective, molto doesn't change (\"very\"). Before a noun, it agrees (\"a lot of\").

È una settimana molto lunga: ho molte riunioni.It's a very long week: I have a lot of meetings.

Two traps: stanco becomes stanchi and stanche in the plural (the h keeps the hard sound). And è (it is) has an accent, while e without an accent means \"and\": la riunione è lunga.

", "

A model typical week

Read this short text out loud. It brings together everything you've seen in the unit: it's the model for the role-play at the end.

Abito a Parigi. Il lunedì mi sveglio alle sette meno un quarto. Lavoro molto e ho spesso riunioni lunghe.I live in Paris. On Mondays, I wake up at a quarter to seven. I work a lot and I often have long meetings.
Il mercoledì finisco presto e nuoto. Di solito ceno alle otto, poi guardo un film. Non cucino quasi mai.On Wednesdays, I finish early and go swimming. I usually have dinner at eight, then I watch a movie. I hardly ever cook.
Il fine settimana mi riposo: dormo molto, leggo e incontro gli amici. È una settimana faticosa, ma il sabato è sempre tranquillo.On weekends, I rest: I sleep a lot, read and meet up with my friends. It's a tiring week, but Saturday is always quiet.

Notice \"gli amici\": Italian often uses the article where English says \"my\". It's natural, and you don't need anything else.

title: Review: describing your week
why: Review of the unit "My everyday life". The learner asked for more time on the present and on sentence structure: with no new rule, this lesson has them put routine, times, frequency and adjectives together into full sentences to describe their week.
